A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SEC/SECViT research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original SECViT classification, detection and segmentation experiments, plus LLaVA+SEC evaluations, ablations and visualizations.

after.justification: v3 retains original SECViT and LLaVA+SEC experimental results in the main text and supplementary material.

M1.justification: SEC's clustering procedure, Equations 1–6, four-stage backbone and interleaved attentive-pooling connector remain unchanged. Table 12 retains all five SECViT architecture specifications, including XL.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ImageNet-1K classification, COCO detection and instance segmentation, ADE20K semantic segmentation, and the same VQA/MLLM benchmarks. Supervised and self-supervised coverage is retained.

E2.justification: v3 removes NAT-T from the Cascade Mask R-CNN comparison (v2 Table 6, v3 Table 5) and CSWin-B from the ADE20K comparison (v2 Table 7, v3 Table 6). ConvNeXt-L, CoAtNet-3 and MaxViT-L also disappear from the ImageNet comparison. Most comparator groups remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The token-output study changes its reported efficiency measure from inference seconds to training hours (v2 Table 14, v3 Table 11). The two- and eight-cluster SEC-DeiT-S configurations are no longer reported, while the four-cluster configuration remains. These changes do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Removing v2 Table 1 loses the SEC-DeiT-S sensitivity comparison across two, four and eight clusters; only the four-cluster row survives elsewhere. Figure 4 decreases from four visualization examples to three. The SECViT cluster-size, token-output, merging-order and complex-scene analyses otherwise remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations or significance tests. The reporting practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: Unique two-/eight-cluster SEC-DeiT-S scores and selected baseline entries are removed. The relocated token-output table replaces 194/126/116/102/94 inference seconds with 21/14/13/11/10 training hours; the 256+1-token speed becomes 1.6× instead of 1.7× under the different measure. Retained accuracy entries match. The XL classification table block disappears, while Figure 2 remains unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations 1–6 are unchanged. Neither version adds formal assumptions, theorems or proofs beyond the retained method formulation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: single-pass semantic balanced clustering, a versatile vision backbone, and an efficient MLLM connector that preserves or improves performance.

C2.justification: v3 deletes Section 3.3's explanation that pruning prevents restoration of the original feature-map shape, whereas SEC preserves tokens and supports dense prediction. The token-output discussion now attributes its efficiency benefit to training rather than inference. Other mechanism interpretations and performance qualifications remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A loses the ImageNet, COCO and ADE20K training-detail paragraphs. Removed information includes optimizer and scheduling choices, batch size, augmentation and regularization settings, detection resizing, learning rates, weight decay and segmentation training resolution. Architecture specifications and some headline settings remain, and training-time reporting expands, but reproducibility documentation is substantially reduced.

R1.justification: Five cited works are removed: RandAugment, CoAtNet, stochastic depth, CutMix and Mixup. No new works are added. Most related-work positioning remains, although the dense-prediction contrast with EViT is shortened.

P1.justification: Ablation and visualization sections exchange order, the token-output discussion moves from Appendix B into the main text, and supplementary material is placed before the references with its own heading. An affiliation is updated and acknowledgements are added. Most retained prose is unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 Table 1 is removed, several tables lose rows, and remaining tables are renumbered. The token-output table moves from a full-width appendix display to a narrow main-text column. Figure 4 moves and drops one example; Figures 1–3 and 5 retain their content.

improvement.justification: v3 preserves the method and most empirical results, but deleting the dataset-specific training details from Appendix A weakens reproducibility, while some useful ablation and comparison evidence is lost. Bringing the token-output study into the main text and expanding training-time reporting provide limited benefits that do not offset these omissions. The overall decline is limited because the central scientific content remains largely intact.
